problems.stem: What is the defining architectural strength of swarm intelligence?
options: Every agent waits for a central commander before acting
Useful global behavior can emerge from simple local rules
The system works only when every agent has full information
A queen node is always required for control
problems.explanation: Swarm systems rely on local interaction rules that scale into coordinated collective behavior.

Indirect coordination through changes in the environment
A centralized scheduling algorithm run by one master node
A method for forcing all agents into one exact path

problems.explanation: The classic boids model is built around separation, alignment, and cohesion.

problems.stem: Why might engineers choose many cheap robots over one powerful centralized robot in a disaster zone?
options: Because distributed systems can remain functional even when many units fail
Because swarms require no sensing at all
Because centralized systems are always impossible to build
Because local rules prevent any communication between robots
problems.explanation: Distributed swarms can be more robust because failure of some units does not collapse the whole mission.
